report.title: Checkout API p95 latency regression caused by sequential per-item pricing calls introduced in deploy d-4821
report.summary: Since ~2026-11-27T17:35Z the checkout-api p95 latency climbed from ~211ms to ~2360ms. A deploy d-4821 (checkout-api v1.4.2) at 2026-11-27T17:34Z introduced sequential per-item pricing calls which increased pricing-service traffic and added ~2s per checkout pricing request.
report.customerImpact: Customers experience slow checkouts (p95 ~2.3s since 17:35Z). Success/error rates remain normal but latency exceeds SLO and may reduce conversions; no duplicate charges or failed payments observed.

rootCause.description: Deploy d-4821 replaced a single batch pricing call with sequential per-item GetPriceAsync calls (one HTTP call per item, per request). Traces show 8–9 sequential pricing requests each ~250ms, adding ~2s to request latency. Pricing-service request rate spiked ~545% starting 2026-11-27T17:35Z.

evidence.detail: checkout-api latency_p95_ms baseline 211ms -> latest 2360ms (change +1016%), change detected startedAt 2026-11-27T17:35Z; pricing-service requests_per_min baseline 2615 -> latest 16878 (+545%), change detected startedAt 2026-11-27T17:35Z.
Deploy d-4821 (checkout-api v1.4.2) deployedAt 2026-11-27T17:34Z by jlee with summary 'Refactor cart pricing to support bundle discounts'.
Deploy diff for d-4821 shows code change from pricingClient.GetPricesAsync(cart.Items.Select(...)) to per-item pricingClient.GetPriceAsync(item.Sku, item.BundleId) in CartPricer.cs (sequential loop).

Distributed traces at 2026-11-27T17:38-17:44Z show checkout-api performing 8–9 sequential pricing-service GET calls, each ~230–294ms, totaling ~2s added: e.g. trace tr_21aec9d947 duration 2528ms with nine sequential pricing spans ~243–294ms each.

recommendedActions.rationale: This is the fastest safe mitigation: revert to prior behavior (batch GetPrices) to restore p95 latency and stop the pricing-service request storm. Timing matches deploy at 17:34Z and latency spike at 17:35Z.
If a full rollback isn't immediately possible, pause any continuing rollout and route traffic to previous stable version instances.

As a medium-term fix: update CartPricer to call pricing-service in parallel (fan-out with bounded concurrency) or restore batch GetPricesAsync; add request-level timeout and fail-open behavior for pricing to avoid blocking checkout.
Add or enable circuit breaker/backpressure to prevent cascading latency when pricing is slow and to return cached/best-effort prices under high latency.
Continue monitoring latency, pricing requests_per_min, error rates and conversion metrics until p95 returns to baseline and traffic stabilizes.

followUps: After rollback, run load test with representative carts including bundles to validate batch vs per-item behavior.
Consider adding a unit/integration test preventing regressions that convert batch calls into sequential per-item calls for N items > 1.
Review deployment process for safer feature flags to gate behavioral changes.
